newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's civil service reform faces panel vote Wed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's civil service reform faces panel vote Wed.

text.p: A constitutional reform of Brazil's civil service will be put to a vote in a committee in the Chamber of Deputies on Wednesday, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Luiz Carlos Santos said.
If approved by the committee, the so-called administrative reform, allowing for the dismissal of currently unsackable civil servants, would progress to the floor of the lower house.

Santos denied speculation that last week's announcement of a package of cost-cutting and tax-raising decrees to reduce Brazil's deficit had annoyed deputies to the point of jeopardising approval of the reform.
Congressmen are traditionally sensitive to the use of decrees by the presidency which, they believe, undermine their role in the democratic process.
"The reform is more than urgently needed," Santos said.

The administrative reform would allow federal, state and municipal governments with payroll spending above 60 percent of receipts to sack categories of civil servants whose jobs are currently protected by the constitution.
It would also set a ceiling of about $10,800 on civil servants' monthly pay and benefits and subject all public sector pay rises to approval by Congress or the state and municipal legislatures.
The reform needs a simple majority of the committee's roughly 30 members to progress to the floor of the lower house.
It remained to be seen, however, if enough deputies would show up and ensure quorum for the vote.
Congressmen have so far failed to return en masse to Brasilia after abandoning the capital to campaign in the first round of voting of municipal elections on October 3.
